Theorem
[Interior Hessian Hölder estimate for concave equations] 1. ch17:17.14\group chapter-17Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0473 Let $u\in C^4(\Omega )$ solve $F[u]=0$, where $F\in C^2(\Gamma )$ is elliptic with respect to $u$, satisfies (17.43), and is concave in $r$ on the range of $D^2u$. For every $\Omega '\Subset \Omega $, egin{equation} ag {17.52} [D^2u]_{\alpha ;\Omega '}\le C. \end{equation} Here $\alpha $ depends only on $n,\lambda ,\Lambda $, and $C$ also depends on $|u|_{2;\Omega }$, $\operatorname {dist}(\Omega ',\partial \Omega )$, and the first and second derivatives of $F$ other than $F_{rr}$. The same conclusion holds when $F$ is convex in $r$.
Proof

\sketch Apply the weak Harnack inequality to the nonnegative deficits of the directional second derivatives in Lemma 35. Concavity supplies the reverse control through the equation itself. For $h_k=D_{\gamma _k\gamma _k}u$, $v=\sum _kh_k^2$, and $w_k=h_k+\varepsilon v$, the differentiated equation and Cauchy’s inequality yield

egin{equation} ag {17.48} F_{ij}D_{ij}w_k\geq -\lambda ar\mu , \end{equation}

with $ ar\mu $ controlled by the stated derivatives of $F$. If $W_{ks}=\sup _{B_{sR}}w_k$, weak Harnack gives

egin{equation} ag {17.49} \Phi _{p,R}(W_{k2}-w_k) \leq C(W_{k2}-W_{k1}+ ar\mu R^2), \end{equation}

where $\Phi _{p,R}(v)=(|B_R|^{-1}\int _{B_R}|v|^p)^{1/p}$. Summing over $k e l$ gives

egin{equation} ag {17.50} \Phi _{p,R}\left(\sum _{k e l}(M_{k2}-h_k) ight) \leq C((1+\varepsilon )\omega (2R)-\omega (R)+ ar\mu R^2). \end{equation}

Summing over all fixed directions then gives an oscillation decay

\[ \operatorname {osc}_{B_R}D^2u \le C\left( rac R{R_0} ight)^\alpha (1+M_2) (1+\widetilde\mu R_0+\widetilde\mu R_0^2), ag {17.51} \]

for concentric $B_R\subset B_{R_0}\Subset \Omega $, with $M_2=\sup |D^2u|$ and $\widetilde\mu $ controlled by the stated derivatives of $F$. Covering $\Omega '$ yields (17.52). Replace $F$ by $-F$ in the convex case.

□

The global structure conditions used for interpolation are egin{equation} ag {17.53} egin{aligned} 0<\lambda |\xi |^2& \le F_{ij}(x,z,p,r)\xi _i\xi _j\le \Lambda |\xi |^2,\ |F_p|,|F_z|,|F_{rx}|,|F_{px}|,|F_{zx}|& \le \mu \lambda ,\ |F_x|,|F_{xx}|& \le \mu \lambda (1+|p|+|r|), \end{aligned} \end{equation} for nonzero $\xi $ and $(x,z,p,r)\in \Gamma $, where $\lambda $ is nonincreasing and $\Lambda ,\mu $ are nondecreasing functions of $|z|$.
